Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verse 5:

It was necessary that, after describing the status of the angels, Allah Himself should also be described:

﴿Rabb as-samawati wal-ard wa ma baynahuma wa Rabb al-mashariq﴾ (38:5) "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and the Lord of all the easts."

These earth and heavens that surround human beings tell them that this vast universe has a Creator and Governor. In this world there is no being, besides Him, who could claim that he has any share in its creation or its management. No intelligent person can escape the acknowledgment that the Creator of this world possesses unrestricted powers. He is the Lord, and He alone is the Owner of the earth and the heavens and everything between them: whether winds, clouds, light, creatures, creatures that can be seen, or creatures that cannot be seen, and about which human knowledge keeps increasing day by day. Yet the majority of them still remain hidden from our eyes.

The distances of the heavens, the earth and the space between them are so vast and so great, and the creatures found between them are so diverse, beautiful and harmonious, that a living-hearted person cannot remain unaffected by them. Without being deeply impressed and taking lessons from this universe and reflecting upon it, only a person whose heart has died can pass by. Therefore such a person is not affected by these pleasing impressions, and his heart and mind do not stir even on seeing these wonders.

﴿Rabb al-mashariq﴾ (37:5) "Lord of the easts." For every star there is an east, and for every planet there is also an east. Therefore there are countless easts in this universe. Within these vast celestial bodies there are uncountable easts. This expression also contains a profound allusion to the earth on which we live. When the earth performs its rotation before the sun, at some time one part of it is east, and at some time another part is west. This process continues one after another. As soon as any part comes in front of the sun, it is east, and the part opposite to it is west. As the movement and rotation continue, the east changes and the west changes too. This is a reality of which people were unaware at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. But Allah gave them this information in such an ancient age.

This is an extremely profound system, according to which the easts move across this earth, and this beauty which spreads over the earth at sunrise is worthy of filling the human heart with pleasant impressions and deep reflection. And a person should cry out how glorious is the Maker of the universe, and a person should cry out that indeed Allah alone is the Creator of the universe, for the signs of this wondrous attribute, its extent and its nature, show that its Maker is One.

For this reason the attribute Rabb al-mashariq is mentioned here. We will soon discuss the stars, shooting stars, devils and their being driven away, and on that occasion will also explain some further meanings and connections of Rabb al-mashariq.

The commentary at the start of this surah dealt with the mistaken views the Arabs held about the angels. Here the discussion turns to their mistaken views about the devils (shayatin).

The Arabs held that there was a kinship between God and the jinn. Some Arabs worshipped the devils for the sole reason that they believed the devils had knowledge of certain unseen matters of the Malakut al-Samawat (the dominion of the heavens). They believed the devils were connected to the Mala' al-A'la (the Highest Assembly, the angelic realm) and could therefore bring benefit or harm. After the mention of the earth, the heavens, and the easts, whether these are understood as the risings of the stars, the risings above the earth, both kinds of east, or as light and illumination, the commentary now turns to the stars.

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾ (37:6). Merely a glance reveals this adornment. Observe what the stars and constellations present on a moonlit night. It becomes evident that beauty is an important element in the creation of the universe. Just as God's creation appears unique upon reflection, it also appears beautiful. Beauty in the design of this cosmos is not a temporary colour; it is a genuine element. Two things are the fundamental material of the creation of the universe: first, a plan of the highest perfection, and second, the most beautiful forms of nature. These two elements are equal and are ends in themselves, and in this universe both perfection and beauty perform their own functions.

On a moonlit night, when a person looks at the sky filled with stars, he is beholding the most beautiful scene in this world. This scene is so lovely that a person may keep gazing, his eyes do not tire and his heart is not dissatisfied. Every star shines and glitters, and every planet scatters its light. A person senses that these are the loving eyes of the cosmos, glancing covertly; when a person looks at them, they close and hide, and when you turn your gaze away, they shine again and remain in search of their beloved gaze. Every night the position of these eyes differs and their destinations vary. This too is a spiritual and psychological nourishment for the human being, and however much one consumes it, one is never satiated, nor does one grow weary.

The next verse explains that these stars have another function. Some of them are piercing meteors (shihab thaqib), and they bombard those devils who attempt to draw near to the Highest Assembly.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 7–10:

"And to guard it against every rebellious devil [﴿وَحِفْظًا مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ﴾]. They cannot listen to the exalted assembly; they are pelted from every side, driven away, and for them there is perpetual punishment. Yet if any of them snatches something away, a piercing flame pursues him [﴿إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ الْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ﴾]."

Some stars are such that they guard the higher world. Their duty is to prevent the devils from gathering information about the decisions made in the higher world concerning this world. Whenever a devil tries to steal a secret from the higher world, a shooting star pursues him, strikes him and drives him away. For such rebellious devils there will be a punishment in the Hereafter that will never end. Sometimes devils do bring some information, and it is these devils that the shooting stars pursue. These shooting stars fall upon such devils and reduce them to ashes.

We cannot fully understand the nature of these matters: how these devils carry out this spying, how they snatch some information away, and how they are consumed by shooting stars. These are matters of the unseen world, and the nature of human understanding and perception is incapable of knowing them, nor can it imagine their reality. Our way is to affirm whatever comes to us from Allah. What we know about physical phenomena in this world is superficial knowledge.

The real point is that these devils are prevented from reaching the higher world, and they are also prevented from listening closely to what happens there. These are the very devils about whom the people of Arabia claimed that they had a kinship with Allah (God forbid). If their claim were true, the matter would have been different; it would not be that the relatives of Allah are repelled, driven away in this manner, and pelted with burning stones if they snatch something. These relatives would come and go freely in the higher world.

After the mention of the angels, the heavens, the earth and what lies between them, and after the mention of the stars with which the heavens were adorned, and after the mention of the rebellious devils upon whom shooting stars are hurled, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is now commanded to ask these people whether they are stronger in creation or the one mentioned above [﴿أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَا﴾]: "Are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?" If the Creator is mightier and more powerful, then why do they become terrified at the thought of being raised again and mock it, and consider its occurrence unlikely? Yet the resurrection of people is no more difficult a matter than the creation of these great and awe-inspiring beings.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 37, verse 11:

فاستفتھم اھم ۔۔۔۔۔ اباؤنا الاولون (11 – 17)

Now ask them: are they harder to create, or are the others We have created? Indeed, We created them from sticky clay. (37:11)

Ask them whether they affirm that the angels, the heavens, the earth, the atmospheres between them, the devils, the stars and the shooting stars are all creations of Allah. Then, is their creation more difficult, or is the creation of these worlds of Allah?

After this question, no one waits for their answer, because the answer is obvious. This question is asked only for rebuke and to express astonishment at their dullness. It is asked because these people are extremely heedless and, to a surprising degree, lacking in understanding. So the reality is placed before them: at the beginning, you were created from sticky clay, and this clay was taken from the same earth, which is one of the creations.

﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.﴾ (37:11) Therefore, these people are not especially difficult to create, nor is their creation hard. Their position is strange: they do not understand their own foolishness. Instead, they mock the signs of Allah. They are warned of accountability through resurrection after death, and they regard it as a joke. It is this foolishness of theirs that causes astonishment in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and yet these people continue on their own course.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 12–14:

"Rather, you wonder, and they ridicule. When they are reminded, they do not take heed. When they see a sign, they dismiss it with mockery." (37:12–14)

It is fitting for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be astonished at their affairs, for he finds Allah in his heart, as every believer does, and he clearly sees the signs of Allah, which are scattered everywhere in this universe. He is astonished that a person could be blind to these signs and these manifest proofs, and how such a person could adopt this ignorant stance.

On the one hand, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is astonished at their attitude. On the other hand, despite the matter being explained so clearly, and despite the issues of the Oneness of Allah and the Resurrection after death being made clear, their hearts are covered with veils and their nature has been distorted. They mock, or rather, they seek out mockery and invite others to mockery. This is expressed by the word (yastakhirun). One example of their mockery and lack of understanding is that they call the Qur'an sorcery and wonder that the Qur'an calls them to the belief in being raised again after death.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 15–17:

وقالوا ان ھذا... ابآؤنا الاولون (37: 15–17): "They say: This is nothing but plain sorcery. Can it be that when we have died and become dust and bones, we will then be raised again, and our forefathers of old as well?"

The mere imagination of it is terrifying, let alone that they would eat from it and fill their bellies with it.

Allah has made this tree a trial for the wrongdoers. When they heard the name of zaqqum, they used to mock it, saying, "How will this tree grow in Hell? Will it not burn?" Some people said so, for example Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, who said in a very jocular manner: "O people of Quraysh, do you know what the zaqqum tree is? Muhammad frightens you with it." They said: "We do not know." He said: "It is dates and butter of Yathrib, and if it becomes available to us, we will surely gulp it down." But how would he know that the zaqqum tree is a different thing, one that humans have not tasted, and they do not know it either.

The commentary passage is an excerpt from Sayyid Qutb's Fi Zilal al-Quran, so I'll translate it as follows.

Verse quoted: ﴿Then, indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.﴾ (37:66)

"And in eating it and in expelling it, they will suffer distress, because it will be like the heads of the devils. Now they will turn to water to quench their thirst, and for drink they will be given impure water."

"Then indeed for them... boiling water" (37:67) — "And after this, these people will rise from that feast and go to their real destination, Hell. What an evil place of arrival and what an evil resting place it is. We seek refuge in Allah."

﴿Then indeed ... al-Jahim﴾ (37:68)

Thus this unique scene comes to an end, and the first lesson of this surah concludes. It is as though this scene is one being witnessed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 69–70:

Lesson No. 209: Explanation of the Verses

69 ... to ... 148

In this lesson, the context of the discourse moves away from the world of the Hereafter, the blessings of Allah, and the punishments of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and now enters into human history and the conditions of earlier nations. The story of guidance and misguidance is taken from the beginning of humanity. This story is one and the same among all nations, and it becomes evident that the deniers of Makkah, who reject the call of Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ), are the remnants and examples of the earlier deniers. They are told that the same thing has always happened before you. In this way, the most ancient pages of human history are placed before their hearts. In these narratives there is also a source of reassurance for the believers, because the entire history of humanity bears witness that Allah has always taken care of the believers.

Accordingly, one aspect of the story of Hadrat Nuh (AS), and parts of the stories of Hadrat Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Musa, Harun, Ilyas, Lut and Yunus (peace be upon them all), are presented to the readers. The conditions of Hadrat Ibrahim and Hadrat Isma'il (peace be upon them) are narrated at somewhat greater length, in which the greatness of faith, sacrifice and obedience, and the concept of Islam that was in the minds of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them), are described here, and in it a link of their story is given which is not given in any other surah except this one. The basic content of this lesson consists of these stories.

"Innahum alfaw aba'ahum ... ibadallahi al-mukhlasin" (69–74).

These people have drowned in misguidance and error, in that in every matter they follow the footsteps of their forefathers. They do not reflect upon any matter that arises. Rather, like hasty people, they keep flying and running on. They keep placing their feet upon the footsteps of their forefathers, without thinking and without using reason. And since those forefathers were misguided, these people too are misguided. "Innahum alfaw ... yuhra'un" (37:69–70): "They found their fathers astray, and they hastened upon their footsteps." The reality is that these people and their forefathers were upon the same misguidance in which most of the deniers were involved.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 37, verse 84:

Among the distinguishing qualities of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) are soundness of heart, rectitude of belief, and sincerity.

﴿Idh jaa'a rabbahu bi-qalbin saleem﴾ (37:84): "When he came to his Lord with a sound heart."

What is a sound heart (qalb saleem)? It is to submit completely before Islam, to hold complete love for Allah, and to have a clean, straight way of life, which is soundness of heart. The expression qalb saleem is deeply meaningful and carries a clear picture of its own meaning. The expression is simple and easy to grasp, and it is also clear. The meaning of qalb saleem includes cleanliness, sincerity, straightforwardness, and purity. The word is very simple, not complicated. It encompasses all the meanings mentioned above, whereas the other words mentioned do not have such comprehensiveness. This is a unique style of expression in the Holy Qur'an.

It was this sound heart that led him to dislike the beliefs of his people. When a person has a healthy way of thinking and is naturally sound in disposition, then, by virtue of the purity of his heart, he dislikes what is disliked, both in thought and in action.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 85–87:

"When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these things that you worship? Do you desire falsehood, gods other than Allah? Then what is your assumption about the Lord of the worlds?'" Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw that they worshipped idols and shrines. Therefore, by the standard of his sound nature (fitrah saleemah), he takes them to task sharply: "What are you doing?"

﴿Ma<u></u>dha ta'budun﴾ (37:84): "What are these that you worship?" That is, what are these things? They are by no means worthy that they should be served, or that anyone should be their servant. In truth, a person cannot be under any misapprehension about them. They are merely fabrications, inventions, and there is no doubt that they are made up. For by worshipping these false gods, you deliberately forge a lie.

﴿Afkan alihatan dona Allahi tureedun﴾ (37:86): "Do you desire false gods besides Allah?" This is what your conception of Allah amounts to. Your concept of divinity is so base that human sound nature rejects it at first sight.

﴿Fama zannukum bi-Rabbi al-'alameen﴾ (37:87): "Then what is your assumption about the Lord of the worlds?" This phrase shows that sound nature rejects, at first sight, any matter that is contrary to reason and conscience, and that human intellect and understanding deny it. Now, the context does not mention any answer from them. What conclusion Ibrahim (peace be upon him) reached through sound nature and a sound heart is told in the next link, because his people were upon hollow, fabricated beliefs.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 88–93:

"فنظر نظرۃ فی النجوم ۔۔۔۔۔ ضربا بالیمین (88 – 93)"

It is related in the narrations that at that time it was a day of 'Eid or of a fair. Perhaps it was Nawroz. On that day people would go out of the city. According to custom, they would place fruits before their idols as a means of seeking blessing (tabarruk). After outings and entertainment, they would partake of these blessed offerings. When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) found a disappointing response to reasonable arguments, and reached the conclusion that the distortion in their beliefs and ideas had become so great that there was no longer any way to reform them, he resolved in his heart to give them a bitter lesson. He waited for that day for his plan, because on that day these people would leave their places of worship empty and go outside, and it would be possible for Ibrahim to carry out his plan. The narrow-mindedness and perverse understanding of these people had become unbearable for Ibrahim. When the other people said to him, "Come with us, leave the place of worship," he looked up at the sky and said that he was unwell. He could not go for outings and entertainment, because outings and fairs are for those who wish to indulge in pleasure, whose hearts are empty and who have no interest or important matter before them. Ibrahim was constantly troubled over the sickness of his people, so when would his sound heart have found joy in outings and entertainment?

Whatever the case, the people were in a hurry to go and celebrate their 'Eid according to their customs and traditions. So they paid little attention to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), left him behind and went off to enjoy themselves. And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) got the opportunity he had been seeking.

Ibrahim immediately went to their so-called gods. Before them were placed various kinds of food and fresh fruit. By way of mockery, he said, "Will you not eat?" It is obvious what answer the idols could give to this mockery. Now he said, with a bit of anger and open mockery, "What has happened to you? Why do you not speak?" Sometimes a person speaks in jest to a thing which he knows does not hear and cannot answer. Even knowing the reality, a person says such things. In truth, Ibrahim was saying this out of frustration with the worthless and false beliefs of these people. Obviously the idols could not and did not answer. Now, instead of his tongue, the hands of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) went into action.

﴿فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًا بِالْيَمِينِ﴾ (37:93) "Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand." Now his sickness, the constriction of his heart and his distress were removed. In other words, his heart was cooled.

A large number of people, indeed the whole fair, assembled. All the people on one side, and one believer on the other side. A single individual who wishes to act. Despite the simplicity and clarity of this argument, people, through their heedlessness and wrong course, did not pay heed to it. It has always been the way of falsehood not to heed the very simple and logical reasoning of truth. And those upon whom Allah has placed the duty of enjoining what is right (amr bil-ma'ruf) and forbidding what is wrong (nahy 'anil-munkar) have always endured oppression from the people of falsehood.

"They said, 'Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire.'" (37:97)

This is the argument of power and force, and fire and persecution are the only argument that tyrants have. Whenever their proof runs out and a tyrant cannot present any argument, he resorts to oppression, especially when the word of truth is presented to tyrants and it silences them.

What happened after their threat, the Qur'an does not specify here, and it is made clear that the people of truth attained success and the deniers remained in loss.

﴿They plotted against him, but We made them the lowest.﴾ (98) ""

When Allah does not wish, what can the plans of weak servants accomplish? And what can weak and insignificant servants do against Allah's affair? The tyrants of the world, its oppressors, rulers, dictators, and their helpers and supporters are nothing in the face of Allah, when Allah's grace is upon His servants.

Now the second link in the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) begins. His dispute with his father and his people has come to an end. They decided to burn him in a fire of their own making, a "hajim" (blazing fire). And Allah decided that they would remain in loss. Ibrahim was saved from their scheme. Here Ibrahim bid farewell to his former life and began a new stage of his life. The file of his previous life was folded up, and a new chapter of his life began.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verse 99:

﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ (37:99)

"I am going to my Lord." This is a migration before the physical migration (hijrah), a psychological and ideological migration. It is a migration in which he is bidding farewell to his entire past and ancestral place. He is leaving his father and his people. He is leaving his home and homeland. He is severing all the ties that bind a person to this earth and to these people. He is crossing every obstacle and moving forward. He is ending all preoccupations. Lightening every burden, he is migrating to his Lord. He is casting everything behind him. He is surrendering his whole self to the Lord and keeping no part of his being for himself. He is certain that his Lord will surely guide him, help him, and show him the straight path.

This is a complete migration, indeed a complete transfer from one state to another. Cutting all ties and attaching oneself to the One Lord alone is, as it were, an act of utmost single-mindedness, detachment, sincerity, and submission, with full tranquility and full certainty.

Abraham was alone at that time; he had no offspring. What he was leaving behind were the relations of kinship and family. He was renouncing every kind of friendship and familiarity. He was abandoning all past attachments and habits. He was severing all the bonds that are formed through one's birthplace. All the ties between Abraham and his household, and those who had resolved to throw him into the fire, were cut. Therefore he resolved upon this determination: "Now I am going to my Lord." And since his family was left behind, he sought offspring and successors in place of relatives.

﴿My Lord, grant me [a son] from among the righteous.﴾ (100)

﴿…﴾ Allah accepted the prayer of this sincere servant of His, who had left everything behind and came before the court of Allah with a sound heart.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 37, verse 101:

﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy.﴾ This is Ismail, as is apparent from the context of this surah and the narrative. And Allah praised his knowledge, his patience and his forbearance, while he was still a boy.

We should pause at this point and reflect on Ibrahim's solitude, his separation from his homeland, and his distance from his kinsfolk, and then imagine the joy at the good news of this child, whom the Lord Himself describes as a forbearing boy. Now the life of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his conduct come into view, which is a unique conduct in the whole of human history, and in his own life it is certainly a memorable conduct. This is the conduct that remains an exalted and sublime example for the Muslim ummah until the Day of Resurrection. This conduct was presented by Ibrahim himself.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 37, verse 102:

فلما بلغ معہ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ من الصبرین (102)

Ya Allah, what a great faith, and what a lofty station of submission and contentment! Here is Ibrahim (peace be upon him), an old man, far from his relatives and kin, far from his homeland and country. In old age and advanced years he was granted a son. For a long time he waited for that child. When Allah gave him this distinguished and capable son and bore witness to his rank and station, the boy was still not fully accustomed to him; he was still a child. He had only just begun to walk beside his father and was near to becoming his companion in life. In short, just as Ibrahim's hopes had become attached to this child, he sees in a dream that he is slaughtering him. Ibrahim understands that this is a signal from Allah that he should sacrifice this child. Now what happens? He does not hesitate at all. He has no doubt and no uncertainty. Only the spirit of obedience comes to the fore. He readily accepts the command of his Lord. Yet this was only a signal; it was not an explicit command, nor had revelation come to him directly. But he considered the signal from his Lord sufficient. For him, a signal was enough. He said "Labbaik" and prepared to carry out the command, without any objection, without any question such as "O Allah, why should I slaughter my only son?"

Ibrahim does not say "Labbaik" in a state of lamentation and distress. No agitation overtakes him. Rather, he is an embodiment of submission and contentment, calm and dignified. This composure, steadiness and contentment of his is revealed in the words in which he presents this proposal to his son. This is indeed a very great undertaking, but his words are extremely serious and his manner is dignified.

قال یبنی انی۔۔۔۔ ماذا تری (37: 102) "Ibrahim said to him: 'My son, I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you. Now tell me, what is your view?'" These are the words of a man who has complete control over his nerves. He is fully at peace concerning the important matter before him. He is certain, and he is determined to fulfil his duty. These are the words of a believer, of a believer whom this great matter does not frighten into hastily doing it, nor into closing his eyes so that he may escape it, the matter may end, and the burden that has fallen upon his nerves may be lifted. It is not like that.

There is no doubt that this act is indeed unbearable. The demand is not that he send his only son into a battlefield, nor that he assign him to a task that will end his life. Rather, the command is that he slaughter him with his own hand. And this command comes to him in a dream. And Ibrahim places it before his only son and asks him to consider the matter and give his opinion.

Moreover, Ibrahim does not suddenly seize his son and slaughter him in a state where he would not even know what is happening and the matter would be concluded. Rather, the matter is placed before him in the form of a proposal, because Ibrahim (peace be upon him) feels that this is the will of his Lord. Therefore, this matter should be carried out in the way that is the will of the Lord. The command of the Lord is to be obeyed with the head held high. Thus the child too should know what matter is at hand, and he too should bow before this command. There should be no compulsion and no constraint, so that he too may receive the reward of obedience, attain the lofty station of submission and contentment, and taste the sweetness of obedience. Let his only son also taste the pleasure of surrendering his life, and let him also see the good which is loftier than life. Now, what is the son's decision? His father has seen a dream and places the dream before his son, proposing that the son be slaughtered. What is the decision? The son is, after all, the son of Ibrahim. He too has reached that exalted station upon which Ibrahim stands.

قال یابت افعل۔۔۔۔ من الصبرین (37: 102) "He said: 'O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.'" Hazrat Isma'il does not merely bow his head before this command; rather, he accepts it with great confidence and filled with the good pleasure of Allah. "Ya abati" – "O my father" – said with the utmost love and the utmost intimacy. He is about to be slaughtered, yet there is no fear in him and no lamentation. His senses are intact, and indeed there is no diminution in his respect and love.

افعل ما تومر (37: 102) "Do what you are commanded." Hazrat Isma'il's feeling is the same as that which his father had before him. The son also understands that the father has received a signal regarding the great sacrifice. And a signal from Allah is also the command of the Lord, and for a prophet of great dignity this signal is sufficient, so that he acts without any hesitation, without any doubt, and without any pretext.

The conversation is taking place in the presence of the Lord of Honour with great respect. The one speaking is fully aware of the limits of his strength and of his capacity to endure. He knows his own weaknesses. Therefore, the help of Allah is sought. For this reason, this sacrifice and this obedience are also attributed to the will of Allah.

ستجدنی انشاء اللہ من الصبرین (37: 102) "You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient." These sons do not display their bravery, nor do they speak in a boastful or reckless manner, nor do they heedlessly rush into danger. They do not show any aspect of their personality here, nor do they assert their size or their weight. They attribute the whole matter to Allah: that if the sacrifice which Allah has demanded is accompanied by Allah's help, and He grants them patience, then the task will be accomplished.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 105–107:

﴿And We called out to him: "O Ibrahim! You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾ (37:104–107)

Your dream was also true, and you made it true, making it so in practice. Allah desires submission and contentment, such that nothing remains within the self that conceals anything from Allah, that is dearer than the command of Allah, or that offers any safeguard against the command of Allah. Even though it was his only son and the beloved of his heart. Even though it was his very life and soul. O Ibrahim, you have indeed shown this in action. You were ready for the great sacrifice. Had Allah not held your hand, you would have sacrificed your most cherished possession. You performed the sacrifice with utmost seriousness, with calm and dignity, with assurance and confidence, with deliberation and reflection. Now only blood and flesh remained. At this station, in place of the blood and flesh of a human being, the blood and flesh of a sacrifice is offered. Its substitute is given, and it is named the great sacrifice. A ram, by the command of the Lord, came beneath the knife of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and he slaughtered it in place of Isma'il (peace be upon him), and it was said:

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ (37:105) We bestow favour upon them by choosing them for such a trial, by preparing their hearts for submission, contentment, obedience and fidelity, by moving them to this momentous task, by granting them the ability and patience for such a great sacrifice, and by rewarding them. And We show them kindness by declaring them deserving of the true reward.

This ordeal and trial has been made a continuing practice (sunnah jariyah). Every Eid al-Adha, the sacrifice continues. It is the lasting memorial of this great event, in which faith is seen at its peak, in which the beauty of obedience and the height and greatness of submission and contentment are seen. The Muslim ummah keeps renewing the remembrance of this sacrifice so that the recognition of the greatness of its forefather Ibrahim may be continually renewed, the one whose creed this ummah follows, whose lineage and whose ideological heritage it inherits, so that it may well comprehend the outlook on life and the beliefs and faiths that are the legacy of the millat of Ibrahim. And so that one who knows it may understand that the Muslim is one who carries out the commands of the Lord, the Exalted, without question or hesitation, gladly. And upon hearing the command of Allah, or rather upon a mere sign, he puts it into practice. He keeps nothing for himself; there is no safeguard. In obeying Allah, he does not adopt his own method or style, but his action arises in accordance with the will of Allah and His way, just as the command is given and just as the command was received.

Then the ummah was also taught this lesson: in carrying out the commands of Allah, harshness and severity upon the ummah are not desired, so that it would be given commands beyond its capacity and strength. Allah gives commands which the ummah can answer with "labbayk" and carry out, and fully discharge. And whatever command comes, it says "sami'na" (we hear and obey), and does not offer any suggestion of its own. It neither shows laxity in it nor boasts of its compliance. When Allah knows of readiness and submission, then He does not take delight in punishing His servants and treating them harshly. Readiness and bowing in submission are in fact counted as action, and the ransom is given in place of the actual act. This is Allah's dealing with this ummah, just as it was with its forefather Ibrahim.

When Allah knows of readiness and submission, then He does not take delight in punishing His servants and treating them harshly. Readiness and bowing in submission are in fact counted as action, and the ransom is given in place of the actual act. This is Allah's dealing with this ummah, just as it was with its forefather Ibrahim.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 37, verse 108:

﴿And We left for him (a good mention) among the later generations.﴾ ”“. For centuries this event has been mentioned. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was made an ummah (a leader of a community of faith). He was made the father of the prophets. He was made the father of this ummah. This ummah inherited his millah (religious way). For this reason, Allah placed upon them the duty of guiding and leading all of humanity. Accordingly, this ummah was made the successor of Ibrahim, until the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 37, verse 109:

﴿Salamun ʿala Ibrahim﴾ (109). Peace from the Lord, the Exalted, comes upon Ibrahim (ʿalayhi al-salam). It is recorded in a Book that is lasting and enduring, like the Noble Qur'an, and thus it is inscribed into the existence of this universe.

Thus do We reward the good-doers. (110) "Thus do We reward those who do good." We give them their reward by putting them to trial and bringing forth their loyalty through it, by perpetuating their remembrance, by sending peace upon them, and by honouring them.

Verse 111 reads: ﴿Indeed, he was one of Our believing servants.﴾ This is the reward for his faith, and its reality is what appeared through his success in this trial. After this, Allah once again bestows His favours upon them, and Allah's generosity comes once more. It takes the form of a second son, Ishaq, being given to them in old age. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is also blessed, and his son Ishaq is blessed too, and Ishaq is made a righteous prophet.

Wa bashsharnāhu bi-Isḥāq... wa-lahu fi-hi mubīn (37:112–113) — "We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous. And We blessed him and Isaac; and among their offspring are the good-doers and those who clearly wrong themselves."

After Ishmael and Isaac, their descendants continue in succession, but the inheritance of their progeny is not an inheritance of flesh and blood. It is an inheritance of belief and religious community (millah). Therefore, whoever remained upon this millah was a benefactor (muhsin), and whoever deviated from the millah and its beliefs was declared a wrongdoer (zalim), and kinship and lineage were of no benefit to him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verse 113:

"And among their offspring are those who do good, and those who clearly wrong themselves." (37:113) And from their descendants were Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 114–122:

{Wa laqad manannaa 'alaa Moosaa ... 'ibaadanal-mu'mineen} (114–122).

In this glimpse of the story of Musa, it is shown that Allah bestowed His favour upon him by choosing him for the office of prophethood, and through him He delivered him and his people. This deliverance was from the great torment in which he and his people had been afflicted. The details are given in other surahs. Here it is only said that Musa and his people were given victory and dominance over the oppressors and tyrants, were given the Book containing clear commands, and were guided to the Straight Path (al-Sirat al-Mustaqim). That is the way which Allah grants to all the believers, namely the Islamic system of life. And the favour upon them is that the mention of Musa and Harun was made lasting. This section also concludes with the expression of peace from Allah upon Musa and Harun. These brief and impactful phrases are repeated again and again, to make it known that Allah bestows favour upon His righteous servants and also grants their remembrance permanence, and to show that the worth and value of the believers is due to their faith and Islam, that is, due to His favour.

Following this, a glimpse of Prophet Elias (peace be upon him). Who was he? The preferred view is that the prophet mentioned in the Old Testament by the name Elijah (Ilya) is the same Elias. He was sent to the people of Syria. These people worshipped an idol named Ba'l. Baalbek is, to this day, among the remains of that idol. The worshippers of Ba'l must have lived there.

﴿And indeed Elias was among the messengers.﴾ (123–132)

Elias called his people to monotheism and criticized them for worshipping Ba'l and for abandoning the One who is ﴿the Best of Creators﴾. ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers﴾ is the same, just as Abraham criticized the idol-worship of his people and his father. In the same way, every messenger came and held his own people to account for their idol-worship.

The result was that the people denied him. Allah, the Exalted, says that they will be seized and brought forward, and they will receive the punishment that is always given to those who deny. Only the believers among them and the sincere servants of Allah will be excepted.

This gathering concerning Prophet Elias also concludes with the fact that peace from Allah comes upon him, he is honoured, and Allah gives such a reward to the believers and the doers of good. The biography of Prophet Elias appears here for the first time, but with great brevity. We too will content ourselves with brevity here. However, one technical point needs to be explained here:

﴿Peace be upon Ilyasin﴾ (37:130). Here a separate "ين" has been attached to the name of Elias so that the musical beauty of the worship is enhanced. This is the particular style of expression of the Qur'an: the verses of the surah typically end with near vocal harmony, and this style of expression has a great impact on the listener.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 139–142:

﴿وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ... ﴿فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾ (139 – 148)

The Qur'an does not mention where the people of Yunus (Jonah, peace be upon him) lived. It is clear from the Qur'an that they lived in some coastal settlement. Narrations state that Yunus's heart was filled with grief because of the continual denial by his people, so he gave his people a warning that a punishment was soon to come upon them. He set out, extremely angry with his people, and went off. He went to the seashore, and there he boarded a ship that was full of passengers. In the middle of the sea, the ship was overtaken by a storm and was caught in the waves. An announcement was made by the people: among the passengers of this ship there is someone who has committed a fault, who is a person upon whom wrath has fallen, and it is necessary that such a person be thrown into the sea so that the ship may be saved. So they cast lots, so that whoever's lot came out would be thrown into the sea. The lot fell upon Yunus (peace be upon him). Among those people, Yunus (peace be upon him) was well known for goodness and piety. But when his name came out of the lot again and again, they threw him into the sea, or he himself jumped into the sea. Then a fish swallowed him. At that time all the people were blaming him, meaning that he indeed deserved blame, because he had abandoned the mission for which he had been sent, and had left his people in anger, even though the guidance from Allah had not yet come. When he realised within the belly of the fish, he began to seek forgiveness for that wrong, and he acknowledged that he had done wrong.

﴿لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ "There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers." Allah heard his supplication and accepted it. So the fish spat him out onto the shore.

Lesson No. 210 At a Glance

The stories brought in the second part of this surah shed light on matters such as the relationship between Allah and His servants. They also show how Allah seized those who denied His messengers, those who served other than Allah and who associated with Allah His own created beings. In the light of the truth that was the subject of the first lesson, this final lesson guides the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hold a discussion with these people on the subject of the reality of their fabricated belief that the angels are the daughters of Allah, set against all these truths. It also concerns the status of their fabricated belief according to which they assume that there is a kinship between Allah and the jinn. It reminds them that you used to wish that a messenger would come among us, and you used to say that if a messenger came, we would accept his guidance wholeheartedly. But now your state is that when the messenger has come, you have adopted a posture of disbelief. The surah concludes with the record that Allah has made a promise to His messengers that they will certainly prevail, and that these polytheists' attributions to Allah are far from Him, and that all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. So it begins.

Lesson No. 210 Explanation of the Verses

149 ... to ... 182

Fastaftihim li-rabbika al-banat ... in kuntum sadiqin (149–157)

This false belief of theirs is encircled from every side. Speech is directed against them in their own language, and the very thinking that existed in their society is used against them. In the Arab society, sons held greater importance than daughters. They regarded the birth of daughters as a calamity. Daughters were considered a lesser creation compared to sons. Yet, despite this, they claimed that the angels are goddesses and that they are the daughters of Allah. Accordingly, this belief was refuted in accordance with their own logic and thinking, so that they might see that, setting aside reality, even by their own accepted standard their belief is wrong.

Fastaftihim li-rabbika al-banat wa lahum al-banun (37:149): "Now ask them: for your Lord are daughters, and for them are sons?" Does this seem reasonable to your heart, when in your society daughters hold a lower rank than sons? What a strange division you have made: for you are sons, and for the Creator are daughters? Or that Allah has chosen daughters for Himself and left sons for you? Neither of these two propositions is correct. How worthless are these assumptions of yours. How did this fabricated thinking arise among you today? From where did this belief spread that the angels are female? Did they witness their creation, were they present at the time, and did they come to know their sex? Am I ... Am (we) created the angels as females, and they were witnessing? (37:150): "Did We create the angels as females while they were witnessing?" Here Allah refutes their saying and belief by quoting it in their own stated words.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 37, verses 171–173:

ولقد سبقت كلمتنا۔۔۔۔ لهم الغلبون (171–173) ""۔ This promise is always true, and the word of Allah stands firm in its place. The monotheistic way of life (nazariya-e-hayat) is established on the earth. The edifice of faith has been completed. Despite all difficulties and obstacles, the word of Tawhid is raised high. Even though the deniers deny, and even though those who raise the banner of the call to Islam and the establishment of Islam in the world are subjected to every kind of oppression, today the beliefs of the disbelievers and their influence have ended from the world. The entire ideological strength of the disbelievers and polytheists has ended. Today, the beliefs and ideologies that are alive in the world are those that the Messengers presented. Even today, the creed of Tawhid presented by the Messengers overshadows the hearts and minds of people. It gives a special quality to people's conceptions and ideologies, and despite all obstacles it is clearly dominant over the hearts and minds of humanity on this earth. And all those ideologies that opposed the monotheistic ideology presented by the Messengers have failed. These ideologies have ended even in those regions from which they arose (socialism in Russia). And the word of Allah's Messengers is still high today, and the army of Allah is still dominant today in ideological terms.

This is a general statement, but there is one matter that is found as a reality across the whole earth, and it has always been found in every age, and that principle holds true for every movement and call: when the callers are sincere, truthful, and single-minded in their call, they remain victorious in every circumstance, no matter how many mountains of difficulties and obstacles are set up in their path. The army of Allah always remains victorious; the sincere ones certainly have to fight various battles and face battles on every front, but the final outcome is always that the army of Allah is victorious. This is Allah's promise: even if the powers of the whole world rise up against it, this promise will be fulfilled. The believing sincere ones will receive help; they will prevail, and their authority will be established on the earth.

Allah's promise is not a partial event but is one of the Sunnahs of Allah in this universe. And the Sunnah of Allah keeps moving in the same way as the stars and planets move in their orbits. There is not a moment's difference in their speed in their orbits, just as there is no disruption in the alternation of night and day. For centuries this alternation has continued. Just as the manifestations of spring and autumn come and go and keep reviving the dead earth, so too the Sunnah of Allah continues to flow. But it is bound by Allah's decree and proceeds according to Allah's will, and it manifests as Allah wills. Sometimes its manifestation appears delayed, and this delay comes because of the desires of hasty humans. But there is no deviation in this Sunnah. Sometimes this Sunnah works in such a way that a person cannot understand it; it comes in a form that is not in a person's imagination. And when the Sunnah of Allah has done its work and passed, after a period the people of faith come to know that help from Allah had worked from such-and-such a quarter.

The army of Allah that follows the Messengers intends that its help come in the specific form that is in its mind. But Allah's will is that this help come in a most excellent and complete form. Thus happens exactly what Allah wills, even though this army may think it is undergoing great hardship, and in its view a long time has passed in struggle, and the waiting has exceeded its imagination. For example, the Muslims intended that at the Battle of Badr the caravan would fall into their hands, but Allah intended that this worldly gain should slip from their hands, and that they should encounter an army and a mighty host, and clash with a group that possessed arms and equipment. And what Allah chose was better; it was better for Islam and for the Muslims. This was Allah's help for the army of God. Allah deals with His armies in exactly this way throughout the whole of human history.

Sometimes the armies of Allah are also defeated in some battle, and the course of the fight turns against them; trials and difficulties also come upon them, because Allah's purpose is to grant victory and dominance in some other greater battle. And Allah knows that at that moment victory is not beneficial for His army, and that at the next opportunity that victory will be very broad, very comprehensive, and will have far-reaching effects.

Allah has stated His word; His promise and His will have already taken effect, and the Sunnah of Allah has been proven again and again.

ولقد سبقت۔۔۔۔۔ لهم الغلبون (37:171–173): "Indeed, Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and that Our army would surely be the victorious."

After this decisive promise, and after it being a most longstanding document and coming from Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is now commanded to leave the polytheists of Makkah. Now see how Allah's promise proves true and how the Sunnah of Allah works. You too wait, and they too wait, and observe the works and majesty of Allah.
